chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muawiya ibn Hukaym, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about al-Nabeez, is it wine? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever increases in excellence (pleasure) upon leaving it, so it is wine.'

key_terms.التَّرْكِ: Leaving it to settle or age
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: A specific type of fermented drink made from raisins or dates, often cited in hadith regarding wine laws
key_terms.خَمْر: Wine or intoxicant, defined here by its effect rather than just its source

ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence define wine based on its changing quality over time?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a functional criterion for *khamr*, defining it by the quality of its intoxicating effect rather than solely by the fermentation process. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that any substance producing the effects of wine is prohibited, extending the ban beyond grape wine to include other intoxicants. It highlights the importance of sensory and experiential evidence in determining the legal status of consumables.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muawiya Bin Hukeym, from Abu Malik Al Hazramy, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,
‘I asked Abu Ja’farasws about Al-Nabeez, is it (classified as) wine?’ so heasws said: ‘Whatever increases in excellence (pleasure) upon leaving it, so it is (classified as) wine’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mu’awiyah ibn Hakim from abu Malik al-Hadramiy from abu al- Jarud who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about al-Nabidh; if it is wine. He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever upon drinking is more pleasurable than not drinking, it is wine.’”
